key_insight: Entropy regularization smooths the Bellman operator, and SmoothCruiser leverages that smoothness to obtain problem-independent, provable sample complexity for value estimation in MDPs and two-player games: O~(1/epsilon^4) for accuracy epsilon.
problem_solved: How to plan and estimate value functions sample-efficiently (with polynomial guarantees) in entropy-regularized Markov decision processes and two-player games given only a generative model — a setting where non-regularized approaches lack known polynomial sample-complexity guarantees.
method: Design of SmoothCruiser: a planning algorithm that exploits the smoothness induced by entropy regularization on the Bellman operator.
Use of generative-model sampling to construct value estimates with controlled approximation error, yielding a problem-independent sample complexity bound O~(1/epsilon^4).
Extension of the approach and guarantees from single-agent MDPs to two-player games by leveraging the same regularization-induced smoothness properties.
impact: Provides a theoretically grounded, sample-efficient planning method for practitioners using entropy-regularized RL or game-solving, informing algorithm design where stability/exploration via regularization is desired and giving concrete sample budgets for target accuracies.
visual_elements: Before/after diagram: Bellman operator (non-regularized) vs. smoothed Bellman operator (entropy-regularized) showing reduced sensitivity
Flowchart of SmoothCruiser: sample from generative model -> smoothing step -> value update -> convergence check
Log-log plot of sample complexity vs. epsilon comparing O~(1/epsilon^4) (regularized) to the non-regularized (no polynomial guarantee) baseline
Schematic game tree/MDP with highlighted sampled transitions and estimated value function to illustrate applicability to two-player games
paper_title: Planning in entropy-regularized Markov decision processes and games
paper_authors: Jean-Bastien Grill, Omar Darwiche Domingues, Pierre Ménard, Rémi Munos, Michal Valko
